last_checked.note: 2026-07-23 check: skipped two intermediate tags (v6.0.0.20 created 07-21, v6.1.0.3 created 07-20 -- latter looked like a hotfix/staging branch based on non-release commit message) and jumped straight to the newest, v6.0.0.21 (created 2026-07-22T23:29:01Z). Verified it reached environment:production across 4 clusters (ap1a, eu5a, us1a, us2a) before treating it as current -- prior run's note flagged that GitHub 'latest' isn't always the real prod release. Cross-checked every error/critical message pattern that looked new against the prior release's own logs (v6.0.0.19, ef47292b): WORKER TIMEOUT (gunicorn), Celery TimeLimitExceeded (chart/dashboard thumbnail generation), ForkPoolWorker SIGKILL exits, 'Filter type not supported for column' (RBAC filter validation), alert query failures, and transient Postgres SSL drops all pre-date this release at comparable or higher rates -- added to known_noise since they're recurring background conditions, not regressions. No genuinely new error signatures found. Six clusters were mentioned in the original 2026-07-16 note vs. 4 seen this run -- worth checking next run whether rollout is still in progress or two clusters were decommissioned.
